findings.claim: the spec still records this chore as outstanding, and the seventeen new tokens are recorded in the design system's own README rather than in a design spec's "DS gaps" table — both are spec-side edits this run is forbidden to make

witness.detail: specs/user-management/README.md:60 reads 'InfoBanner hardcodes its four tone triplets as literal oklch(...) values rather than tokens ... promoting them to tokens is the outstanding design-system chore before spec 03 adds more banners.' After this diff InfoBanner.jsx holds no literal at all (grep -rn 'oklch(' '1_DS for dev/components/' returns nothing), so that sentence describes a state that no longer exists. Line 54 of the same file says 'DS gaps — anything missing from the design system is added to the design system, not improvised per screen, and recorded in that design spec's "DS gaps" table'; the five scale steps and twelve --banner-* tokens are recorded only in '1_DS for dev/README.md' line 88. Neither can be fixed here: scripts/static-gate.mjs rule 1 (pipeline/spec-immutable, scripts/static-gate.mjs:57-67) halts any run that edits a file under specs/. This is the deliberate design — the spec changes first, by a person — so it is a note, not a block. It sits with the pre-implement notes P1 and P2, which the same edit can close.

findings.suggestedFix: in a separate, human-authored change: replace the line-60 paragraph with the closed state, and record the five scale steps and the twelve --banner-* tokens in the DS gaps table of the design spec that owns the banner (02-authentication-login.design.md)

findings.claim: the new e2e case carries an id that appears in no spec, because the handoff minted it

witness.detail: CLAUDE.md:62-63 — 'Test cases are numbered in the specs (`TC-01-E2E-03`) and the code references those ids.' git grep 'TC-DS-BANNER-E2E-01' matches only e2e/tests/ds-info-banner-tones.spec.ts and this run's own .workflow files; no spec numbers it. The handoff says so itself ('The id is minted by this handoff because the chore carries no TC list', handoff.json T6). The alternative available to the implementer was to ship no guard at all, which would leave requirement 2 — every rendered pixel unchanged — pinned by nothing, so the test is the better of the two. The convention is still unmet, and only a spec edit can meet it.

findings.suggestedFix: when F1's spec edit lands, number this case in the design spec that owns InfoBanner so the id has a home, or rename it to that spec's numbering

findings.claim: the branch carries no commit: HEAD is the base ref, so `git diff <baseRef>...HEAD` is empty and this review was performed against the working tree

witness.detail: git log --oneline -1 on spec/ds-infobanner-tokens prints d4b6afc, which is exactly run.json's baseRef, and `git diff d4b6afc...HEAD --stat` prints nothing. The whole change is staged/unstaged in the worktree instead ('1_DS for dev/tokens/colors.css', InfoBanner.jsx, _ds_bundle.js, _adherence.oxlintrc.json, _ds_manifest.json, 1_DS for dev/README.md, e2e/tests/ds-info-banner-tones.spec.ts). I reviewed `git diff d4b6afc` (base against worktree), which is the same content; QA and anything else that reads base...HEAD will see an empty diff and could report a vacuous pass.

findings.suggestedFix: commit the change on spec/ds-infobanner-tokens before QA reads the diff

findings.claim: the worktree also carries pipeline changes that are in none of the seven planned tasks, so a PR cut from this branch would ship them with the token promotion

witness.detail: Beyond the seven planned files, `git status` shows package.json (adds the 'ship' script), scripts/ship.mjs (new, 273 lines), scripts/wf.mjs (+154: a `wf watch` command, richer status/log, and AUTHORITY.implement = ['spec']), .claude/agents/implementer.md (+33) and .claude/skills/ship/SKILL.md (110 changed).
